english: You turned around. There stood / Bertin, the dwarf warrior you / met at this level's entrance.
My my, adventurers these days / are just as tough as we were!
Don't know what they are, but / these crystals seem to hold the / thoughts of an ancient demon god.
That's why the monsters guard / places like this. They hold / them as holy ground.
Takes me back. It took us months / on end to beat the / likes of them.
We'd get hurt, crawl back to / town, stock up on items, and / dive right back in. Over and over.
Can't count how many times those / fellows beat us to a pulp.
Look at the scars on this face. / Every one of them was their / work, back in the day.
Bertin winked like a naughty / child and grinned.
That's why you came to this / crystal chamber too, eh?
So, how did it feel, taking the / monsters' Allied Action for / the very first time?
What's that? You're not taking / me for a ride, are you?
Allied Action is mastered only / by monsters that have killed / each other for ages untold.
If it were that easy for us to / learn, we'd have had no / trouble at all!
Come to think of it, I heard / some strange rumors on the / way here. Many times.
Word that the Knights of Duhan / had mastered Allied Action, / or some such tale!
I didn't give it a second / sniff. Sounded ridiculous / to me.
I always wondered how folk / reach the lower levels so / easily these days.
And watching you fight, there's / something different from the / way we used to do it.
I'm no learned man, but when it / comes to fighting, I've got / an eye for detail.
Now then. What in blazes is / Ortrud up to, and why the / silence? Best find out.
That's right, that's right! We / were amazed at first too - / gaining a demon god's power.
The flow of those coordinated / moves, and the killing blows / born out of them.
No need for words, not even a / glance. All of us moved as / if we were one creature.
Back then I felt we wouldn't / lose even if a Gold Dragon / came at us.
But even in those days, Ortrud / was an odd one.
Know what he said, back when we / were living our simple, / happy days?
'With this, peace will come / back to Venoa.' That's / what he said.
we brought down the unbeatable / Black Knight of San-Goth.
Ah, that reminds me. I hear some / fool went and raised the / death spirits again.
Walked the labyrinth a bit and a / whole swarm came at me. / Annoying as all get-out!
Must be some fool who knows / nothing of how Black Knight / William met his end.
When I find the one who did it, / we're going to have a nice / long talk, believe me!
Well then! Can't let you beat / me. I'd best push on and / head deeper myself.
Bertin strode off, his body / swaying like a barrel / of liquor.
A torrent of countless / thoughts came flooding in.
The thoughts of monsters that / ruled this lair, ever craving / power, filled the crystal.
And at the end of those grim / thoughts shone one record, / bright as a jewel.
It was the memory of a demon / god from ages long past.
Mmph! That's it, I can't! Too / hot! It's coming off!
With that, the orc gripped his / own neck two-handed and / heaved with all his might.
Inside the sagging orc head / was Yoppen's own!
He tugged the bandana free and / mopped his sweat-soaked / yellow face, panting.
Whew! Thought I was gonna die! / Why's the heat change so much / just one floor down!?
And princess, you don't have to / go holing up in this / labyrinth, you know~
Call me the patient prince, / jerked around on purpose / by his selfish princess.
Ah well, since I'm here, I'll / just take a dip over there!
Yoppen leapt straight / into the pool.
Hyaa~, it's cold! Cold! / It feels so good~!
Whew! Thought I was gonna die! / Why's the heat change so much / just one floor down!?
And princess, you don't have to / go holing up in this / labyrinth, you know~
Call me the patient prince, / jerked around on purpose / by his selfish princess.
Awww, there used to be a / spring here. Now it's gone!
And I came all this way for / a dip! What a rip-off!
Wiping away sweat, Yoppen / shouldered his gear and / walked off.
Seeing the empty water tank, / Raiman began to speak.
Hmm!? According to the map, this / tank should be the famous / sight of this floor!
You explained to the puzzled / Raiman about the lever needed / to explore this floor.
Oh, I see! So there was a / hidden device beneath us!
Just what you'd expect of a / true adventurer. Listening to / you, I can feel the adventure!
Still, I did so want to see the / witch's water that never / dries up in this heat.
That said, no use lingering / here any longer!
I'm so looking forward to it. / After all, that War God is / still down there, isn't he?
Inside, an imp sprawled on the / floor, reading a book.
This here's big bro Ingo's / secret hideout! Don't you / dare barge in here!
So this is Ingo's hideout that / Lidi spoke of. No doubt / about it.
You told the imp about / Lidi's request.
Hmm, so that's why you're here. / Business with big bro / Ingo, huh.
But bro ain't here now. Fact is, / he almost never comes back / to this place.
After all, bro's a legendary / treasure hunter, always / running the labyrinth!
Too bad for you, though. I got / orders from bro about / that thing.
If it weren't his orders I'd / kick you right out, but I / got no choice!
The imp clicked his tongue / in frustration.
Then, grudgingly, he took out / the request note he'd gotten / from Ingo and showed it.
Fine. Then do like bro says: / bring me a Thief's Mask, the / kind them midgets wear.
Do that, and I'll trade you the / thing bro left with me!
Oh yeah? I don't give a damn / what you do!
But 'til you take bro's request, / no way his key ends up in / your hands!
Knew it! Came crawling back to / take bro's request after / all, huh?
Fine. Then do like bro says: / bring me a Thief's Mask, the / kind them midgets wear.
Do that, and I'll trade you the / thing bro left with me!
My anger gauge shoots up every / time you spout another / dumb joke, pal!
Yep, that's the mask the / Leprechaun folk wear, / no mistake.
Tch! Galls me to hand it to some / shady drifter I don't know / from nowhere, but...
Bro's orders are orders. Take / it and be grateful!
That key's bro's handiwork, made / with heart and soul! Don't / you dare treat it rough!
There, business done, right? / Then scram! And don't / come back!
You had no Thief's Mask to show. / The imp shook his head.
What the hell, man! Just catch a / Leprechaun or two and snatch / their masks already!
Time sure flies. Twenty years / already, since that day!
A dwarf warrior stood there, / gazing fondly at the statue / of a goddess.
Noticing your eyes on him, the / dwarf came over, scratching / his head sheepishly.
Strange! That statue used to / face sideways. Now she's / facing front!
Dunno who moved it, but don't / you think it looks better / this way?
Feels that way to me, anyhow. / Yeah, it's better now / for sure!
Well, I suppose none of that / matters much to you, eh.
The dwarf warrior gave a / friendly smile and a big, / hearty laugh.
I'm Bertin, of Gnome Valley. / Pleasure to meet you.
Funny, though. Is it a sign of / age, that the old days feel / so dear to me now?
Those were the best days of my / life. Lately they even show / up in my dreams!
They were all good folk, every / one of them with a dream / of their own.
We fought like mad to build a / land where everyone could / live and laugh together.
But that war took / most of them!
The dwarf warrior let out / a heavy sigh.
Now it's just me and / Ortrud left.
And him, becoming king and all. / Can't have been easy on him.
Curse or whatever it is, they / say he's grown too weak to / even move about freely.
By rights I ought to be at his / side, helping him, but...
ever since that business, I've / kept my distance from him!
The man who came back from / Banquo was like a whole / different person.
Seems the old king of Duhan and / the nobles betrayed us / at Banquo.
I don't know the details. I was / off leading a detachment / against the city of Toul.
But what he did was wrong! War / or no war, there are things / you just don't do.
He spoke no further, but dark / memories of the past were / plainly crossing his mind.
In revenge for that betrayal, he / hanged near a hundred nobles / in the land of Kadina.
When I heard, I felt sad, angry, / helpless, all at once!
What did we fight for? Wasn't it / to make everyone happy? / That's what I thought.
Betrayed or not, there's no / right to kill those who / hold no sword.
I'd had enough of it all. I went / home and holed up in / Gnome Valley.
Oh, sorry, sorry! Turning / gossipy is a sign of / age too.
The dwarf warrior walked away / humming a tune, his big frame / swaying as he went.
The rubble-choked room was thick / with a foul stench and an / eerie, heavy air.
It smelled of a burnt-out fire, / and sharply of scorched air.
A faint whiff of bloodlust told / that a battle had been / fought here.
You rushed over and propped / the old mage upright.
To think the great mage / Wesbell had only such lousy / servants at his disposal.
Proof that mages and their magic / don't always progress with / time, is it not?
Why not borrow the strength of / those adventurers there for / the next round?
Perhaps they could even / put a scratch on me.
The old mage raised his worn, / exhausted body and spoke.
I learned I was no / match for you at Irikia, / ten years past!
Once I challenged you rashly, / and it cost me my sight / and my right arm.
While the mage strained to / speak, the witch listened / serenely, arms lightly / crossed.
I wish to know. What / is it that you desire?
You hold deathless life and the / deepest secrets of magic. / What could you still seek?
Kingdoms fall and it leaves you / empty. No power, no treasure / can fill your heart.
What do you search for, / wandering through that / eternity of time?
There is nothing you could not / take, if you wished it.
I have not long to live. Let me / die knowing at least that. / What do you seek?
Heh heh heh... I expected better / of the great mage Wesbell. / How foolish.
What do you hope to draw out of / me, the one they fear / and call a witch?
Shall I tell you a heap of lies? / You may pick whichever one / you fancy.
Then die in the dark of death, / tasting nothing but despair.
Lies have ever been the / tools of the weak.
Now, will you not tell me? What / do you wish for? What do / you seek?
A strange tension flowed between / the mage and Aurora.
Nothing could be read from / the witch's face.
That, from a man who knows light / and dark, who even followed / a demon god?
Either way, it is nothing I / could tell your kind.
If there is such a thing as a / god, go and ask him.
With those cryptic words, / Aurora vanished.
No use! I no longer have the / strength left to pursue her!
Adventurers... will you hear / one wish of mine?
The lowest depth of this / labyrinth! Where Aurora / dwells, and all the brood / of darkness gathers.
I pray you reach that place, and / lay hands on the truth in / my stead.
The old mage dragged himself / away and was gone.
The demon god's memory / became yours.
The demon god's memory / became yours.
The demon god's memory / became yours.
Things don't look too good, / do they?
An elf adventurer noticed you / and came over.
Just now, Sir Webster went / heading down, wearing a / mighty proud look.
Seems the lord gave the order to / undo the seal on the / holy beasts.
And with that Cardinal Langobalt / going along, there's no / doubt about it.
It's not as if he doesn't know / that man's true colors!
This Langobalt is a papal / guardian, an enforcer of / the divine power.
Put simply, a mage who summons / holy beasts in the name / of God.
'Holy beast' sounds fine and / well, but they're just the / Papacy's pet monsters.
The adventurer frowned, lost / for a moment in thought.
The name's Uli Ernst. For now, / one of the strike force, / same as you.
I used to be with the / Papacy myself, so I know / just how they think.
So if they've come all the way / out here, risking danger,
it means this Duhan has / something juicy in it / for them.
That's why no town welcomes / the Papacy's meddling.
How can a man like Ortrud / not see it!?
With a deep sigh and a sorrowful / look, Uli walked away.
Raiman and Jill's cold stares / pierced your back.
No doubt because you haven't yet / shown them this floor's / famous sight.
The heat here is a cut above / the rest of the floor.
This must be where the lava / burns hottest on this level.
Dip Fudo's sword in the lava? / Yes / No
You dipped the sword's blade / into the lava.
The blade glowed red with heat, / yet did not warp or melt. It / seemed to drink the heat in.
Whether by its rare steel or the / labyrinth's magic in the lava, / the blade shone brighter still.
A strangely sorrowful air / hung about its glow.
You drew the shining blade from / the lava and wrapped it in / the cloth once more.
You met the Orc who works / part-time at the shop.
The Orc remembered your face / too, and trotted over / happily.
H-hello dere~! You remember / Oda? Oda's doin' his / part-time job!
So happy~! Did ya come all dis / way 'cause ya worried about / Oda an' friends?
Oda an' friends will work hard! / You work hard too, senpai!
The Orc happily went / back to work.
Don't play dumb with us! / Yeah! The sooner you show us / the way, the better for you!
Two orcs stood surrounded by / vicious-looking thugs.
B-but we dunno what yer talkin' / about! // We SAW you! Walkin' round with / a real beauty, and she sure / weren't no adventurer!
Yeah, no mistake! That's gotta / be the woman Webster's after! // N-no, yer wrong! / Dat was just a succubus!
Don't screw with us! / That's it, I've had enough! / I'm gonna kill you both!
Backing away, the two orcs / spotted you and cried / out in joy.
The orcs scurried behind / your backs to hide.
The hell are you!? This ain't / your business, so butt out!
Or what, you mean to cross us, / the Black Snake Squad?
Dung Snakes, was it? How / stupid! What a lame name!
Yeah! An ugly, smelly squad like / yours is a crime against / humanity!
Enraged, the thugs attacked!
The orcs hiding in the shadows / made sure it was safe, then / poked their heads out.
Will more of them keep coming / after us like that!?
Seems Webster's got all sorts of / adventurers hunting for her.
What do we do now? This may be / too much for us to handle / alone.
I'll ask just in case, but you / DO know who we are, right?
It's all 'cause adventurers are / such dirty rats that we're / stuck with this mess!
They get blinded by gold and / help the villains. That's / why we suffer so!
So said the two orcs, / glaring right at you.
How about we have her wear an / orc costume, same as ours?
Might stink a little, but hey, / a smell never killed anyone!
Okay, decided! We're all going / with the orc disguise!
Overthinking everything - / that's our bad habit, huh!
Satisfied at last, Lute and / Emilia bustled off through / the door, chattering away.
Such a beautiful face! Turning / toward the voice, you saw a / lovely woman shimmer forth / from the rock wall.

Weary of this fleeting life, / never knowing true love, / dying without a trace... // Come to me, come... / Let us sleep in the cold dark, / for the darkness hides all... / Do as your heart desires... // To think you could fell the / bewitched Succubus. You have / grown strong indeed.
His battle over, Belgrano / approached you with a smile.
My, how you've grown / in the time since we / last met.
As if you'd walked the line / between life and death many / times over.
I can't count how often the / monsters nearly did me in / before I reached this floor.
Cowering before a rushing horde / of monsters... I looked / pathetic, and comical!
My arm has gone embarrassingly / dull, I fear.
Belgrano said it with a / cheerful, wry smile.
I was raised on battlefields. / This labyrinth's bristling / air oddly puts me at ease.
Swinging a sword suits me far / better than scowling on a / seat back at the castle.
Come to think of it, I still / never plan for the morrow. / That much hasn't changed.
In the war twenty years back, I / gathered orphans like myself / and ran a band of rogues.
We robbed gold and goods from / wicked men and played at / being justice itself.
Had I never met His Majesty, / I'd have been killed and / buried somewhere long ago.
Belgrano, even / in doing good, be as cunning / as the devil.
But with casualties mounting / like this, I cannot idly wait / for the right moment.
Even if it goes against the / code of the Knights.
Around Belgrano there was no / sign of the Knights who / should have escorted him.
Sensing the question on / everyone's face, Belgrano / went on.
I stand here now not as captain / of the Knights, but purely / as one man.
His Majesty decreed the Knights / must wait until adventurers / reach the eighth level.
I know not his reason. Knowing / him, there is some deep / design behind it, but...
I grew tired of waiting. So / here I am, ahead of everyone, / in the labyrinth.
If someone must do it, then let / it be me who breaks through / to the eighth level.
And if I fail, the loss is one / reckless fool. Nothing the / realm cannot bear.
Opening the door, you found a / sour-faced woman inside, / counting her gold.
Honestly, were prices really / this cheap in the old days?
Where I come from, this kind of / coin wouldn't even cover / a bar tab.
The woman heaved another deep / sigh and changed the subject.
Ah, enough of this gloomy talk! / The name's Vago. Lady Vago / of the Flames.
You came here 'cause you want / the Id Bracelet, / am I right?
Well, for reasons of my own, I / won't be moving from here / for a while.
Come again if you want it. I've / got a favor to ask of / adventurers myself.
Oh, you're back. Decided you / want the Id Bracelet after all?
What? Then what in blazes did / you come back here for?
no bracelet, no / business. There's nothing / else for you here.

The old days really are / backward through and / through, eh.
When I picked this up, the / memory of an Allied Action's / use flowed into my head.
But it's the most common Allied / Action there is. I know it / already. Useless to me.
You lot can only learn Allied / Actions this way? How sad / is that!

Truth is, my orc henchman / has gone missing.
Believe it or not, the two of / us were sent here from / the future!
Well, I don't need the likes of / you to believe me. It's the / truth all the same.

I want to get home quick, / back to my own world.
So the pig and I split up to / search for a way back. And / he never came back.
He can't have wanted to settle / down HERE, so I doubt he / ran off on me.
I've been looking myself, but / I just can't find him!
But from a rusty locked room on / the fifth floor, I hear / strange crying sounds.
I can't shake the feeling it's / his voice. Trouble is, I've / got no key.

Well, come back when you find / your spine. I'll be here / a while yet.
Oh, you'll do it? Well, / that's a relief!

As promised, the Id Bracelet is yours.
Vago slipped the bracelet off / her own arm and tossed / it over.
We're heading for the lower / levels now.

Got the Blessed Chainmail!
The Id Bracelet from / Vago began to shine.
The light poured someone's / memories straight into / your mind!
As ever, Vago and Casta / were in the room.
Oh, so you came! Does that mean / you'll take us to the / crystal room?
Wonderful! I knew you'd / come through!
It's on the tenth floor, that / much seems certain. You only / need lead us there.
We'll follow along behind you. / We won't get in the way!
What, you didn't come to / take our request?
If you're going to show your / face, at least come ready / to take the request!
In my mind, Aurora was a witch / who killed on sight, no / questions asked.
She must have known we're with / the strike force, yet she / did nothing. So...
are we not yet strong enough / to be worth her notice?
True, I expected some raging / berserker, so this was a / bit of a letdown,
but Aurora struck me as one with / no interest in anything / outside her own purpose.
My my, our first meeting, / and who knew the witch would / be such a comely young / maiden!
But having met her, I find the / mystery of her draws me more / than the terror.
Not, mind you, because I / have an eye for women!
As Wesbell said, if we learn / what she desires,
it will be our finest weapon / for breaking Aurora.
If you would win a battle, find / what the enemy wants most / of all.
I don't know why. It's been / there ever since I first / saw Aurora!
Is it that icy bearing of hers / that makes me feel so?
She lives on and on, spurning / every salvation God offers...
But her face, when told there / was nothing she could / not have...
it looked for all the world like / she was begging for God's / help!
A witch indeed, and a / mysterious one at that.
A rabid dog that bares its fangs / at everything is far easier / to handle.
As Wesbell asked: what / does she desire?
Magic, gold, eternal youth... / she has all of it.
If she wished, she could take / not just Venoa but the whole / world in her hands.
Struck by some thought, Iris / fell silent a moment, / pondering.
The resurrection of the dead... / a beloved someone lost long / ago, or a beloved child...
Well, that is all I can think / of, if it were me.
Stepping onto the fifth floor, / you saw a band of alchemists, / and Webster at their center.
The Royal Knights are to be / dealt with on sight!
Let no one near who would / hinder my work. Understood?
Webster was briskly issuing / orders to the alchemists.
Webster noticed you / and came over.
Welcome to Dialant, / the city of legend.
We stand upon the elven city of / old, which met its end seven / thousand years ago.
How long I have waited for this / day, ever since word of / ancient Dialant reached me!
And standing here at last... it / stirs the heart, does / it not?
Until now, only a handful ever / reached this floor.
But thanks to your strike force / securing the route down,
even I could make the descent. / You have my gratitude.
Now I go to wake the / sleeping giant god.
The god who, they say, destroyed / this ancient city in a / single night.
Webster's gaze turned distant, / as if fixed on something / far away.
I have longed for it! Ortrud, / who pacified Venoa and leads / the peerless Knights called / the Holy Kings,
and the Black Knight, King of / San-Goth, who leads the / dread Dracul Knights!
But at long last, the means to / raise a sword of my own is / within my grasp.
O Duhan, land of the dead! This / dirge shall see you to / heaven, or to hell!
Unable to contain his / excitement, Webster strode / briskly away.
A sickening stench of blood. / Corpses of adventurers and / monster flesh lay everywhere.
